description: Known authorization and request-security holes (SEC-01): each entry is a known-holes test that asserts the safe behaviour against a real assembled app and fails today. Each reason ends with the finding it records: 'audit <area> #n' is the n-th finding of that area in the rebuild audit, 'critic <theme> missed #n' the n-th missed root cause in that design theme's critique, 'design <theme> RC n' that theme's n-th root cause. The closing package removes its entry with the fix; holes closed before SEC-01 are passing tests in the same files and have no entry.

test: known holes: a throwing authorize is a reported fault

failure.message: the resource authorize failure reached onError
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: createResourceHandlers (core/src/api/resource.ts assertResourceAuthorized) turns a throwing authorize into a silent 403; the fault never reaches the app's onError. Finding: audit core-http #22.

test: known holes: a throwing authorize is a reported fault

failure.message: the readiness authorize failure reached onError
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: mayShowDetails (core/src/server/readiness.ts) swallows a throwing readiness.authorize: the caller sees the aggregate status and the fault is never reported. Finding: design auth-authorization RC 2; audit framework-improvements #9.

test: known holes: a grant does not outlive a demotion
refuses a new admin-only subscription on the same socket after a demotion

failure.message: a demoted user opened an admin-only subscription
failure.name: AssertionError

entries.reason: The transport decides a subscribe with the user resolved at the handshake (or the last revalidation, every 60 s by default), so a demoted user still opens admin-only subscriptions on the same socket until the next revalidation. Finding: audit pkg-content-io #12 and #30; design auth-authorization RC 6.

test: known holes: a tenant-scoped publication stays inside its tenant
delivers a subscriber its own tenant's rows and nothing else
entries.reason: Delivery is not tenant-aware (the fan-out key has no tenant), so the service refuses any publication over a tenant-scoped model outright: it fails closed, but a tenant cannot have live data at all. Finding: critic content-realtime-io missed #1 (live has no tenant model).

test: known holes: a throwing publication authorize is a reported fault
denies the subscription and reports the failure
entries.reason: authorizeRequest (packages/live/src/live-service.ts) catches a throwing publication authorize and answers unauthorized without calling onError. Finding: design auth-authorization RC 2; audit framework-improvements #9.
